title: IWMAC Designer panel file
description: The file Insert JSON… takes and Export JSON writes (format iwmac-designer-panel, version 1), made by the userscript from the same tables its in-file guide writes. An agent returns one such file per panel, raw JSON, counts equal to the array lengths; for a new picture, its drawing in panel.image_svg. That one file is the whole answer: no .svg, .ai, .png or archive beside it - Insert makes the picture from image_svg, and Background → Illustrator writes the .svg and the .ai.

format.description: File type marker, always "iwmac-designer-panel". Checked before anything else is read; any other value is refused.

generator.description: Who produced the file: "IWDIE v<version>" for an export. Write your own agent name when you generate or modify a file.

contents.description: What this file holds: each key's size and use, the -for-ai.png, Insert's check of the file. Read it first. The importer ignores it.

ai_guide.description: This guide (guide_version 2). The importer ignores it. Keep it as it is when you return a file, or omit it; never edit it.

source_plant_id.description: The plant the panel came from; the same value as panel.plant_id. Informational.

panel_name.description: Copy of panel.panel_name for readers; keep the two equal.

panel_width.description: Copy of panel.panel_width for readers; keep the two equal.

panel_height.description: Copy of panel.panel_height for readers; keep the two equal.

counts.description: {single_objects, containers, graphics}: the lengths of the three arrays in panel. Recompute after adding or removing anything; the importer warns when they disagree.

summary.description: Facts derived from this panel at export time (object types, linking, units, z-index values, extent). Read it to orient; drop it or recompute it when you return a changed file, because a stale summary misleads the next reader.

overview.description: The plant behind the panel at export time (v1.62.0), for drawing or linking an overview picture: its units, the rows of their parameters, the tagged signals, this panel's links checked against them, and the picture's layout and style, as tables {cols, rows}. Read overview.read_me first; its rows are the plant parameter source. The importer ignores it; leave it out of a file you return.

background_embedded.description: true when image_data carries the background picture.

background.description: What the image_data blob is (field, mime, width, height, bytes, source_name) so it never has to be opened.

panel.description: The panel document itself, the only part the importer draws. See schema.panel.

image_data.description: The background picture as base64, one very long line, deliberately last. Copy it byte-for-byte; omit it only from a new file with no picture to keep. Never retype, re-encode or edit it. Older exports carry it inside panel instead; both places are read.

image_svg_trace.description: A coarse vector trace of the background, for reading where things are (see structure). Input only: the importer discards it. Never copy it into image_svg.

change_log.description: Optional. When you modify a file you may append entries {when, by, change} here. It is the only sanctioned place for notes; the importer ignores it.

panel.description: The panel document itself, the only part Insert draws.

plant_id.description: The plant the panel belongs to ("3157"); "" for a plant-neutral template. The plant number is also the prefix of every parameter driver_id on that plant.

panel_name.description: The panel name as the Designer shows it.

panel_width.description: Canvas width with the px suffix; "1400px" on a standard panel. Without it the panel size is not applied on insert.

panel_height.description: Canvas height with the px suffix; "750px" on a standard panel.

org_image_name.description: Server-side name of the background picture; "" when the panel has none.

saved_by.description: Who saved the panel. Write your agent name when you create or modify a file.

single_objects.description: Free objects placed directly on the canvas, in creation order. See schema.object_entry.

containers.description: Grouped objects (table rows, room cards). [] on most panels. See schema.container.

graphics.description: Opaque host graphics records. Preserve verbatim; never author one; [] on almost every panel.

converted.description: Present as "true" when a background picture is embedded in image_data. Allowed: "true".

object.description: One object: the same 17 fields on every entry of single_objects and of containers[].items, in this order.

obj_id.description: Which palette object this is (its type). An exact id from object_catalogue in this guide or copied from an existing object; an unknown id draws nothing at all. Case and underscores matter.

name.description: Sequential label "object_0", "object_1", ... in array order, no gaps or duplicates within single_objects. The importer renumbers it on insert, so it carries no identity: never match objects between files by name.

id.description: A host type marker, identical on every object. Not an identifier and not a parameter id. Never change it. Allowed: the literal "driver_id".

posWidth.description: Box width. Copy it from an existing object of the same obj_id; never derive it from how wide the text looks.

posLeft.description: X position from the left edge of the canvas (of the container, for a container item). Emit a plain number: a missing or non-numeric value silently lands the object at 0, and a string such as "120px" is read as 120.

posTop.description: Y position from the top edge of the canvas (of the container, for a container item).

zIndex.description: Stacking order; higher paints on top. Copy the value used by objects of the same role in this file. "default" makes array order the stacking order, so a label emitted before a duct disappears under it. Allowed: an integer as a string ("110"; a negative one, "-445", lies under every other object, as the fleet's room popups carry their frame), or "default".

tag_text.description: The visible caption: an instrument code ("RT401 °C"), a header, a label. Objects that show only a value or a symbol ignore it. A single space " " is the palette default on live-value widgets and null occurs on container items; preserve either exactly and never turn one into the other.

linked.description: Whether the host treats the object as bound. Real exports say "true" on every object, because the host sets it on load whenever driver_id is not the literal "driver_id", even when driver_id is empty. A newly authored unlinked object says "false". It proves nothing about whether the binding is valid. Allowed: "true" or "false".

link_name.description: Host bookkeeping: the literal "link_name" on exported objects, "" on newly authored ones. Never a panel name or a destination.

link_tag.description: IWMAC system tag written by the host tagger (the Tag column of the parameter export); "" or "NA" on most objects. Copy it, never compose one.

sub_group.description: Parameter instance letter ("A", "B") from the parameter source (its SGR column); "" when not tagged.

driver_id.description: The parameter binding: the full plant-prefixed parameter string, "<plant_id>_<DRIVER>_<address>", copied verbatim from one row of the plant parameter source (its Driver ID column). "" on an exported object that is not linked; the literal "driver_id" on a newly authored unlinked object; on sub_page_* navigation objects the numeric id of the target panel ("16"). Never construct, edit, translate or guess one.

unit_id.description: The unit (controller) the parameter belongs to, as the Designer's UNITS list names it and the parameter export's Unit ID column carries it ("V01", "2180", "000:111"); "" when not linked. The literal string "undefined" occurs in real exports; preserve it.

unit_ref.description: Optional stable unit reference; "" in practically every export. Leave it as found.

alias_text.description: What the signal is, in words: the parameter description shown to the person who links the object, and the key by which a whole panel is relinked on another plant. "new text" is the Designer default on unbound scaffold objects; keep it.

container.description: A container of objects (table rows, room cards), as the host writes a plain objects_container.

id.description: Container kind; "objects_container" on every production container.

unique_id.description: MUST contain "custom_" ("custom_30"). A container whose unique_id lacks that substring is silently dropped on insert; the host renumbers it anyway.

type.description: Layout type. Allowed: "container_c" (content only), "container_hc" (header + content), "container_hcf" (header, content, footer), "container_cf" (content + footer).

container_type.description: Flavour. A table_container carries extra keys (num_of_rows, num_of_col, descr_width, val_width, cells, last_y, header_descr) that must be preserved and must not be added to an objects_container. Allowed: "objects_container" or "table_container".

className.description: CSS class; equals container_type on production containers.

header_footer.description: Header and footer rows as {type: "header" or "footer", text, function: "none", function_id: "none"}; an empty array on a plain container.

linked.description: Host bookkeeping; "0" unless the container is bound to a unit.

width.description: Container box width. Metadata, not a clip: items may extend past it.

left.description: X position of the container on the canvas.

top.description: Y position of the container on the canvas.

zIndex.description: A JSON number here (4), unlike objects, where it is a string.

items.description: The objects inside the container: the same 17 fields as single_objects entries, positioned relative to the container. See schema.container_item.

title.description: Custom attribute the host adds; "Objects Container" on production containers.

drawing.description: The panel's picture as vectors (authored on Maskin, Oversikt and Energi; on Ventilasjon only for what no Designer object makes; never on curve, list or room-control panels). The root is the panel's size: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1400" height="750" viewBox="0 0 1400 750">. Every element at the top level is a layer group with an id and a data-name, in this order: <g id="Bakgrunn" data-name="Bakgrunn">, <g id="Ror" data-name="Rør">, <g id="Former" data-name="Former">, <g id="Tekst" data-name="Tekst">. One element loose at the top, or opacity, a filter or a mask on a layer group, and VectorCraft opens the whole drawing as one layer. Each piece of equipment is a group with an id of its own beside its data-name (<g id="Former_MT1" data-name="MT1">), or a house symbol placed by name (<use data-iwdie-symbol="Kompressor" x="120" y="80"/>). VectorCraft names only what has an id, and dissolves a group without one that holds a single thing. Pipes are stroked paths with fill="none", one sub-group per circuit in Ror; a flow arrow is a small filled path of its own, never a marker. Text stays <text>, its font-family, font-size and fill as attributes; never outlines. Hide with display="none", never visibility="hidden". No <image>, <script>, <foreignObject>, <style> or CSS classes: fills and strokes are attributes. A prefix such as xlink: is declared on <svg> (xmlns:xlink) or not used; Insert refuses one that is not. Insert makes the drawing the panel's picture as a sync from VectorCraft does - a PNG that keeps the drawing, uploaded to the plant's pictures - so Edit in VectorCraft opens its layers, Background → Illustrator writes them as an .ai, and Export JSON hands it back as panel.image_svg, stamped data-iwdie-drawing. A drawing Export handed over carries data-iwdie-drawing on its root, and may hold the picture under it as an <image>.

contents.description: What the file holds and where. Reading material: Insert ignores it.

read.description: Each key: its size in kB, its use and what it holds.

overview.description: The plant behind the panel, read from the Designer at export time (v1.62.0). Reading material: Insert ignores it.

objects.description: Every object once: id (o0... as the -for-ai.png marks it), name, obj_id, role, its box on the canvas (x, y, w, h), text, alias_text, unit_id, link, check, the pill (P#) and house symbol (S#) it belongs to, its caption, its container (c#).

bindings.description: Each linked object read against its unit's rows.

style.description: The picture's colours, pipes, pills and text, measured.

objects.description: The kinds of object the panel uses.

symbols.description: House symbols, S1... in this order.

object_looks.description: IWMAC objects the picture shows as pixels: obj_id, box, and the object (o#) on each, null where the panel lacks one.
